# rayl

> An MCP server for Apple Mail, written in Rust. It lets AI assistants search, read, and
> draft with the mail already on a Mac — no API, no OAuth, no rate limits, nothing leaving
> the machine.

rayl reads Apple Mail's local SQLite envelope index and `.emlx` message files directly. An
agent connected over MCP can search mail metadata fast, read downloaded bodies, list
mailboxes and labels, save drafts to Mail's Drafts folder, and export attachments. It cannot
send mail, cannot delete or modify existing messages, and never touches the network.

## Key facts

- Licence: MIT
- Platform: macOS only, verified against Apple Mail V10
- Protocol: Model Context Protocol (MCP) over stdio
- Language: Rust
- Source: https://github.com/oti-adjei/rayl
- Setup guide: https://github.com/oti-adjei/rayl/blob/main/docs/mcp.md

## Tools

- `search_mail` — find mail by subject, sender, recipient, body text, mailbox, flags, date
- `read_message` — read one message's headers and body
- `list_mailboxes` — mailboxes and labels available for filtering
- `mail_status` — which accounts are loaded, what's readable, and why
- `draft_message` — save a new draft in Mail's Drafts (never sends)
- `draft_reply` — save a threaded reply draft (never sends)
- `save_attachment` — list attachments, or write them to files

## Limits, stated honestly

- Search, reading, mailbox listing, attachments, and reply drafts use Full Disk Access
  granted to the app that launches rayl. New drafts can use Mail Automation alone.
  Both draft tools require Mail.app to be running.
- Body search is linear and unindexed; messages Mail stores as headers-only cannot be
  searched (37% of messages on the author's own store).
- rayl persists nothing between requests in the current mode.

## Roadmap

- Indexed body search — an index so body search scales past a few thousand messages (next)
- Script source — planned read modes using Automation permission scoped to Mail.app.
- HTTP transport — reach the Mac's mail from elsewhere (planned)
